summary: Docker discovered on 25 April 2019 that an intruder had accessed a Docker Hub database holding data on nearly 190,000 users (under 5 percent of users), including usernames, some hashed passwords and tokens linking automated builds to source hosting. Docker revoked tokens and told users to change passwords.

overview.background: Docker Hub is a public container registry that offers automated builds from linked source repositories using stored tokens.
systems: Source-hosting tokens for automated builds (two providers)
overview.impact: Nearly 190,000 users were affected. Docker described it as a subset of non-financial user data.
overview.severity: A security incident disclosed within days of discovery.
overview.gaps: The article does not say how the attackers got in or mention builds being disabled.

diagrams.title: A database holds credentials that reach source code
diagrams.caption: Per The Hacker News, the database had usernames, some hashed passwords and tokens for linked repositories; Docker revoked tokens and access keys.

nodes.label: Tokens could reach linked source repositories

diagrams.title: Limit what a stolen database yields (conceptual)
diagrams.caption: General controls: scoped tokens, strong hashing, monitoring of unusual access.

timeline.e: An intruder accesses a single Docker Hub database.
Docker revokes tokens and access keys for users whose autobuilds may be affected.
Docker notifies users and The Hacker News reports nearly 190,000 accounts.
Users change passwords and reconnect autobuild repositories.
Docker reviews policies and strengthens security processes.

rootCause.trigger: An intruder accessed a single database.
rootCause.underlying: The article does not say how.
contributing: Tokens linking builds to source hosting were stored in the database

evidence.label: Docker's description
evidence.body: a subset of non-financial user data
evidence.note: From Docker's statement as quoted by The Hacker News.

evidence.label: Docker's action
evidence.body: acted quickly to intervene and secure the site

diagnose.step: Identify the database and data fields.
Check linked source repositories for odd activity.

verify.step: Check security logs on linked accounts.

fix.safety: If you use automated builds, check for unexpected commits before rebuilding images.

troubleshoot.scenario: A registry you use reports a database breach that included build tokens for your source hosting.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do?
hints: What do you tell users of your images?
troubleshoot.answer: Change passwords, reconnect with new tokens, check repository logs and image digests, and tell users if images may have been affected.

rootcause.q: About how many users were affected?

design.prompt: Design registry integrations that limit token risk.
design.answer: Short-lived tokens, narrow scopes, encryption at rest, access monitoring and fast revocation.
